newsitem.title: USA: Spot US propane rises on Midwest demand.
newsitem.headline: Spot US propane rises on Midwest demand.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices were led higher in midday trade on Thursday by demand in the Midwest and forecasts for possible wintery precipation this weekend, players said.
In Conway, Kansas, spot propane traded at the start at 79.50 cents and then jumped up to 80.00 cent and 84.00 cent deals by midday.

The rise came following a weather report that forecast colder temperatures in the region for Saturday and possibly Sunday. Retailers also began to snap up volumes ahead of an industry holiday event later this afternoon that may keep many players out Friday.
Conway brought up spot prices in Mont Belvieu, Texas, by 2.25 cents to between 56.50 cents and 57.00 cents a gallon. Traders reported small volume deals done in the range.
Meanwhile, normal butane values sagged in line with lower motor gas and lack of demand by refiners.
Belvieu normal butane fell 2.00 cents to 55.50/56.00 cents and Conway material slipped a half cent to 57.50/58.00 cents.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1631
